meta.convert.title: Sensitivity converter · handspan
meta.convert.description: Convert in-game mouse sensitivity between games using cm per 360° and DPI. Shows the source count and in-game verification status for each coefficient.
convert.lede: Enter a game, DPI, and sensitivity to see how far you move the mouse for one full turn, and the sensitivity that gives the same physical distance in other games.
convert.dpi2: DPI to use in another game
convert.basis: Calculated from the DPI you set · Not verified in game
convert.dpiNote: Based on DPI {dpi} · hip-fire horizontal turn
convert.fixPrompt: Fix the inputs above and the other game sensitivities will appear here again.
convert.warnOne: {game} has a coefficient from a single source. Measure one full turn in game before relying on it.
convert.howFormula: cm/360 = 914.4 ÷ (DPI × sensitivity × yaw). Yaw is the angle turned per mouse count at sensitivity 1. 914.4 is 360° × 2.54.
convert.howExclusions: ADS and scope multipliers, mouse acceleration, and per-game field-of-view settings are not included. Only horizontal hip-fire rotation is matched.
convert.howStatus: Every value is an estimated conversion that has not been measured in the real game. The number of sources is shown, but converter sites may copy the same list, so their independence is not verified. Deadlock, Marvel Rivals and PUBG (conflicting values) and Battlefield 6 (non-linear sensitivity) are left out until resolved.
err.dpiRange: Set the DPI to a value between 100 and 32000.
meta.find.title: Find sensitivity · handspan
meta.find.description: Test candidate sensitivities or DPIs in alternating order to find a cm per 360° range that fits your hand. Shows measurement confidence and the verification status of each game coefficient.
find.lede: Keep your current DPI and change only the test sensitivity to find the turn distance (cm/360) that fits your hand. After a warm-up, two rounds fire three candidates in A·B·C·C·B·A order, then show the in-game sensitivity for each DPI. It takes about 10 minutes.
find.pcOnly: Desktop browser with a mouse only
find.dpiHint: Keep your mouse DPI at the value above during the test. The page calculates and simulates the candidate sensitivity or DPI.
find.rangeHint: {lo}–{hi} in Overwatch eDPI. The default range is 43.5–66 cm. If a fast setting felt uncomfortable before, start slower than that.
find.rawPending: Input mode is checked when you start
find.rawOk: Raw input in use · Windows pointer speed has no effect
find.rawWarn: Raw input not supported · Set Windows pointer speed to 6/11 and turn off ‘Enhance pointer precision’
find.progEmpty: No records yet. Once you start, each round adds A·B·C scores and aim endpoints here.
find.histEmpty: No results are saved in this browser yet.
find.belowCands: Candidates are hidden as A·B·C. Knowing the number makes your hand chase it.
find.ovReadyX: Check the game, current mouse DPI, and test range on the right, then press ‘Start test’.
find.warmX: This does not count toward your score. Loosen up with 10 targets and 10 seconds of tracking. Pressing the button locks the mouse to the screen and starts after 3 seconds.
find.trialX: Hit {flicks} targets quickly, then follow a target moving left and right for {track} seconds.
find.feelT: Test {label}, how did your body feel?
find.feelX: Even a good score is not worth pain. Answer honestly.
find.roundDoneX: Check the scores and endpoints in the progress table, then continue.
find.finalX: In-game sensitivities by DPI are in the result panel on the right. Try them in game for a few days before deciding.
find.lockFailT: Wait a moment and press again
find.lockFailX: Right after you leave with Esc, the browser blocks locking again for about a second. A desktop browser and a mouse are required.
find.pauseX: Press again to continue from where you stopped. Paused time does not enter the record.
find.scoreNote: Score = flick (hit rate ÷ median time) 50 + tracking 50, normalized to the best value in the round. The endpoint is where your first aim movement stopped. 1.00× is exact; above 1 overshoots (too fast) and below 1 undershoots (too slow). Candidates marked with body strain are left out of automatic selection.
find.noiseNote: Noise (difference between two runs of the same candidate) ±{n} points
find.warmNote: Warming up. This does not count toward your score.
find.finalMid: Middle value {cm}cm. This is a starting point, not one right answer. Use it in game for 1–2 weeks before deciding.
find.basisNote: Calculated from the DPI you set · Not verified in game
find.fixNote: DPI is rounded to a step of {step}, and cm/360 is calculated from that set DPI (not measured). You have to change DPI in your mouse software yourself.
find.epHigh: Your aim endpoint passed the target by {pct}% on average. Your sensitivity is a little fast. Start with the slower end of the range ({cm}cm) in game.
find.epLow: Your aim endpoint stopped {pct}% short of the target on average. Your sensitivity is a little slow. Start with the faster end of the range ({cm}cm) in game.
find.epOk: Your aim endpoint matched the target distance well ({ratio}×). Start from the middle value.
find.painNote: You also marked body strain at this value. Check your posture (elbow support, shoulder height) before changing sensitivity.
find.reliabilityGood: First and second place differ by more than the noise, so they are distinguishable
find.reliabilityHard: First and second place differ by less than the noise, so they are hard to distinguish
find.dpiNote: DPI values your mouse supports natively, such as 800 or 1600, are a safe choice. If your current DPI is comfortable, keep it and change only the sensitivity.
find.deskBody: It measures mouse movement, so it does not open on phones or tablets. Open the same address on a PC. You can still use the sensitivity converter here.
find.errDpi: Enter a current mouse DPI between 100 and 32000.
find.errFix: Enter an in-game sensitivity greater than 0 to fix.
find.errRange: Enter a cm/360 range between 10 and 150.
find.errGap: The slower end must be at least 4cm above the faster end to split candidates.
meta.click.title: Click accuracy · handspan
meta.click.description: Measure hit rate, missed clicks, and time to acquire targets of different sizes and distances. Only runs with the same conditions are saved and compared in this browser.
click.lede: Practise clicking targets of different sizes and distances quickly and accurately. Hit rate, missed clicks, and time to acquire a target are shown separately.
click.pcOnly: Desktop browser with a mouse only
click.deskBody: It uses the mouse cursor, so it does not open on phones or tablets. Open the same address on a PC. You can still use the sensitivity converter here.
click.esc: pause · results are saved only in this browser
click.pausedBody: Paused time does not enter the record. Continuing resumes from the remaining {s} seconds.
click.distHeading: Time to acquire by target distance (median)
click.cond: {size} · {speed} · {dur}s · includes browser, mouse, and display latency
click.again: Run again with the same conditions
click.empty: There were no clicks to record.
click.insufficient: Hit at least 5 targets to see median values. With fewer hits, distance bins are also marked as too few samples.
click.histHeading: Past runs with the same conditions
click.histEmpty: No past runs with the same conditions yet.
click.belowWhat: The time from a target appearing to the first click that hits it, the number of clicks outside the target, and the share of clicks that hit. These three numbers cannot replace one another, so they are not combined into a single score.
click.belowGame: Games where you pick a target with the cursor, such as League of Legends, and games where you move through menus and inventories quickly. It does not mean your sensitivity or screen matches the real game.
click.belowHist: Records from another PC or different conditions are not compared together. Only runs with the same conditions are shown in this browser.
convert.tolNote: When the current DPI and the game's sensitivity steps cannot get within 3% of the target, we show the closest value and its error and leave it out of the recommendations. 3% is a temporary tolerance, not a verified perceptual threshold.
find.reason.allExcluded: Every candidate was marked uncomfortable, so there is nothing to recommend.
find.reason.insufficient: Too few hits to compare the candidates.
find.reason.indistinct: The gap between the top candidates is smaller than the difference between two runs of the same candidate, so they cannot be told apart.
find.roundNoWinner: This round: no value chosen by measurement
find.noneX: Change the range or check your posture, then test again. Values marked uncomfortable are not offered again.
find.undecidedX: The measurements did not separate the candidates in this range. The range is not narrowed; try the least uncomfortable value in it in the real game.
find.manualNote: The final round value was picked by hand, not by score.
meta.kite.title: Move and attack alternation · handspan
meta.kite.description: Alternate between a move point and an attack target and measure order errors, wrong targets, and the gap between clicks. It does not reproduce any real game's attack speed or movement. Only runs with the same conditions are saved and compared in this browser.
kite.lede: Practice pressing a move point, then an attack target, then the move point again, in order. Order errors and wrong targets are counted separately.
kite.pcOnly: Desktop browser with a mouse only
kite.deskBody: It uses two mouse buttons, so it does not open on phones or tablets. Open the same address on a PC. You can still use the sensitivity converter here.
kite.esc: to pause · results stay in this browser only
kite.pausedBody: Paused time is not counted. When you resume, {s} s remain.
kite.cond: {size} · {speed} · {map} · {dur} s · includes browser, mouse, and display latency
kite.copyFail: The link is selected. Please copy it.
kite.empty: There were no clicks to record.
kite.insufficient: The median gap needs at least 6 successful switches to be reliable. This run had fewer.
kite.histEmpty: No earlier runs with the same settings yet.
kite.belowWhat: Accuracy while alternating between a move point and an attack target, order errors from pressing the wrong button, clicks on the other target, and the gap between successful clicks. These numbers measure different things, so they are not combined into one score.
kite.belowGameH: How it differs from a real game
kite.belowGame: This practice does not reproduce any game's attack speed, movement, or cancel behavior. It uses only original shapes, with no characters or maps from a specific game. It only practices alternating move and attack clicks with the cursor.
kite.belowHist: Only runs with the same settings, including the button assignment, are shown together in this browser. Runs from another PC or other settings are not compared.
find.errNoCands: With this DPI and sensitivity, fewer than two candidates in this range can be set. Find a suitable DPI on the converter page or change the range.
find.reason.noCandidates: Not enough candidates can be set to narrow the range further.
common.invalidArena: The practice area changed size during the run, so this result was not saved. Keep the window size fixed and try again.
meta.index.title: handspan · Mouse sensitivity converter and aim practice
meta.index.description: Convert sensitivity between games, calculate cm/360°, find a sensitivity range with a short test, and practice click accuracy and move/attack alternation in the browser. No install or sign-up.
home.h1: Match mouse sensitivity by the numbers, then check it by hand
home.lede: Convert sensitivity between games at the same turn distance, narrow down a range that suits your hand with a short test, and practice cursor control. No install or sign-up.
home.convert: Enter a game, DPI and sensitivity to see the mouse distance for one full turn (cm/360°) and the matching sensitivity in other games.
home.find: Keep your current DPI and shoot alternating candidate sensitivities to narrow a cm/360° range that suits your hand.
home.click: Click targets of different sizes and distances, with accuracy, missed clicks and time to acquire shown separately.
home.kite: Practice the order and accuracy of alternating move and attack clicks. It does not recreate any real game.
home.noteCalc: Conversions use published game coefficients. Measurements include browser, mouse and display latency, so try a result in the real game for a few days before settling on it.
home.noteData: Each game shows how many sources its coefficient has and whether it was checked in the real game. No game has been checked in-game yet.
home.notePrivacy: Practice records stay in this browser. Nothing is sent to a server.
notfound.title: Page not found
notfound.body: The address changed or the page does not exist.
meta.about.title: About and sources · handspan
meta.about.description: What handspan stores, which external requests it makes, the limits of its measurements, and where each game coefficient comes from.
about.lede: What is stored, what is requested from elsewhere, and where the numbers come from.
about.privacy1: No analytics or ads of our own. Practice records and settings stay in this browser (localStorage) and are not sent to a server.
about.privacy2: Fonts (Archivo, IBM Plex Mono, IBM Plex Sans KR) are served from this site. No requests go to Google or other external servers. Font licenses (SIL OFL 1.1) are in assets/fonts/LICENSES.md.
about.privacy3: The hosting service that serves the site may keep ordinary access logs.
about.measure1: Results include browser, mouse and display latency. They are not the same as in-game performance.
about.measure2: The finder gives a starting range, not an answer. Try it in the real game for a few days before settling.
about.measure3: The 3% target tolerance and the 0.25 s stall threshold are temporary values, not verified ones.
about.sourcesLede: Values are copied as written on converter sites. Those sites may copy the same list, so their independence is not verified. No game has been checked in the real game yet.
meta.ogAlt: handspan: mouse sensitivity converter, finder and aim practice
about.measure4: An end-to-end run with a real mouse has not been verified yet. The measurement logic has only been checked with automated tests.
err.cm: Enter a cm value between {min} and {max}.
err.sensRange: This sensitivity gives a turn distance outside {min}–{max} cm. Check the value.
convert.profErrName: Use a name of 1 to {max} characters.
convert.profErrFull: You can save up to 20 settings. Delete one and save again.
convert.profErrQuota: Could not write to browser storage. Keep a share link instead.
convert.profUnavailable: Saving is not available in this browser (for example, private mode). Conversion and share links still work.
convert.profCorrupt: Some saved settings could not be read and were skipped.
convert.profPrivacy: Settings are stored only in this browser (localStorage) and never sent to a server. A share link contains only the numbers and game you entered.
convert.shareManual: Automatic copy is blocked. Copy the link from the box below.
convert.check1: Enter the sensitivity in game and make sure mouse acceleration (including Enhance pointer precision) is off.
convert.check2: Put a ruler next to the mouse or mark a start point on the pad, and aim at a distinct point on screen.
convert.check3: Slide the mouse slowly sideways until you turn exactly once and land on the same point, and measure the distance.
convert.check4: Compare it with the cm/360 above. If it is off by more than 3%, check the DPI setting, acceleration and the game coefficient.
convert.checkLimits: This matches horizontal hip-fire rotation only. ADS and scope multipliers, field-of-view settings and vertical multipliers work differently in each game and need separate matching.
meta.sens.title: Game-to-game sensitivity conversions · handspan
meta.sens.description: Conversion factors and tables between Valorant, CS2, Overwatch 2 and Apex Legends, matched for the same mouse distance per 360° at the same DPI.
sens.lede: For common game pairs, the factor to multiply by at the same DPI and a table of typical sensitivities. For any other pair, the converter shows every supported game at once.
sens.note: Each factor is the ratio of the two games' yaw values (degrees turned per count at sensitivity 1). None has been measured in the real game.
meta.pair.title: {from} to {to} sensitivity (× {factor}) · handspan
meta.pair.description: To convert {from} sensitivity to {to} at the same DPI, multiply by {factor}. Includes a sensitivity table, cm/360, the formula, sources and limits.
pair.lede: If you keep the same DPI, {to} sensitivity = {from} sensitivity × {factor}. The same mouse distance then turns you the same angle in both games.
pair.updated: Yaw values checked {checked} · not verified in game
pair.tableNote: {to} values are rounded to the step the game accepts ({decimals} decimals). Rounding differences of 0.05% or more are shown in brackets, and anything over 3% is marked in yellow. The factor itself does not depend on DPI.
pair.calcBody: For a value not in the table, a different DPI, or other games, use the converter. If you are not sure which sensitivity suits you, the sensitivity finder can narrow it down.
pair.formulaBody: cm/360 = 914.4 ÷ (DPI × sensitivity × yaw). {from} uses a yaw of {fromYaw} and {to} uses {toYaw}, so at the same DPI {to} sensitivity = {from} sensitivity × {fromYaw} ÷ {toYaw} = {from} sensitivity × {factor}.
pair.dpiBody: If you also change DPI, multiply once more by (old DPI ÷ new DPI). Going from 800 to 1600 DPI halves the sensitivity.
pair.sourcesNote: Values and dates checked on public converter sites. These sites may copy the same list, so their independence is not verified.
convert.profErrInvalid: Fix the inputs first. Settings that cannot be calculated are not saved or shared.
